mapping: Cylinder around a vertical axis through "center" (world metres, +x south, +y up, +z west). Image column u (0 = left edge) maps linearly to azimuth: az = azimuthDeg[0] + u * (azimuthDeg[1] - azimuthDeg[0]); azimuth is measured from +x (south) toward +z (west), so a texel at azimuth az lies in world direction (cos az, 0, sin az). Image row v (0 = bottom) maps linearly to height on the cylinder: y = center.y + radius * (tanElevation[0] + v * (tanElevation[1] - tanElevation[0])); horizonV is the row of the camera horizon (eye height = center.y). Seen from "center" the image is an exact reprojection of the photos (verified by rendering it back to the photo cameras). center = the photo camera position (from the window frame in the photo). suggestedWidth/Height = arc length and height of the cylinder segment at radius suggestedDistance; any radius gives the same picture from center, the radius only sets the parallax when the viewer moves (≈ distance of the main subject).

backdrops.notes: Living-room view south over the lawn to the river (~60 m), the red boathouses (~150 m, az -12..-4), the houses on the far bank (az 0..+14) and the hills (1-2 km). Shot through the west living-room window; window frames, the lamp reflections and the terrace (deck, railing, stair, concrete landing: build them in 3D) are removed. The big lichen rock (3-5 m, az +7..+27) and the trees west of the house (az +15..+66) are close: they only line up from near "center". Keep 3D ground within a few metres of the facade (terrace, a strip of lawn) – the photo itself shows the lawn falling ~2.7 m below the floor down to the river; a ground plane further out would cover it. Beyond az -66 (east, behind the annex) and +66 (west, only seen at grazing angles) the photos are continued by a stretched, softened reflection. Use an unlit material (MeshBasicMaterial, colorSpace SRGB, toneMapped false, fog false) and scale its colour with daylight.

Same geometry as sor.jpg (swap the map or cross-fade). Deep-blue sky with a faint glow low in the south-west (az +40..+90), darkened landscape, the river mirroring the evening sky and a few lit windows in the houses across the river. For night, darken it further (colour x 0.15-0.3).

Kitchen-end view ("ost" = the east end of the room): what the long kitchen window (win-k1, wall x = 6.32) sees from the kitchen island. NB the kitchen windows face SOUTH (like the living room), not east, so facing is "south" and the azimuths are absolute: the "east" part is the dark wooden annex/outbuilding that closes the terrace to the east and fills the left of the view (az < -15, its gable edge runs from az -18/e +13 down to az -12/e -3). Then the river with the red boathouses and the houses climbing the far bank (az +10..+40). The terrace railing, chair and table are removed (build them in 3D); below the railing top (e < -5.5) there is a soft green slope only meant to be seen between the slats. Sky = the same sky model as sor.jpg (same directions), so the two match where they meet. Optional: sor.jpg alone also works for the kitchen windows (it is the same landscape seen 8 m further west); use ost.jpg if you give the kitchen its own backdrop layer or for a kitchen photo comparison.

TV-room strip window (win-tv, wall x = 0, sill 1.64 m): yellow birch leaves close to the glass (left, az 135..160), the light grey-blue commercial building with a flat roof and a mesh fence (~20-30 m), a small spruce, and the forested knoll behind (right). Objects on the sill are removed. Above the photo the knoll/crowns are continued with a rounded top; below the sill only a blurred fill (hardly visible: the glass starts at 1.70 m).
